column4: Removed the servants and women of the household (only Abraham is named, 23:2), the bier, lamplight and dusk; Abraham mourns before his covered dead (23:2-3).
Removed the field and cave shown beyond the gate (not in view in the text), the stone benches and the morning; Abraham bows to the sons of Heth (23:7).
Removed Ephron pointing to his field (not in view in the text), the bronze balance and the midday heat; Abraham weighs the silver before all at the gate (23:16).
Removed the servants carrying the body on a bier and the household procession: the text has Abraham bury Sarah (23:19). The trees at the field's borders kept (23:17).
Removed the great oak (none in the text here) and the camels and herdsmen filling the camp; only Abraham and his servant as he swears (24:2-9).
Added the servant's men (24:32, 24:54); he prays in his heart (24:45), not with lifted hands; removed the city walls and the amber low sun.
Added the servant's men (24:32); removed the servant's staff, the walls of Nahor and the sunset glow; evening, as the text says (24:11).
The servant bows his head (24:26), not to the ground; removed the stars and the lamps on Nahor's walls; added the servant's men; the earring 'upon her face' (24:47).
Removed the household servants doing the work (the text has only 'he ungirded his camels', 24:32), the torches and Rebekah watching; added the servant's men (24:32).
Merged 24:33-41 and 24:42-49 (one moment). Removed Rebekah, her 'grey-haired' mother and the household; Bethuel, who answers (24:50), is there; added the servant's men (24:32, 24:54).
Removed Bethuel and the household from the giving (24:53 names Rebekah, her brother and her mother), the fire and cedar chests; the mother's age isn't given.
Added the servant's men (24:54); removed the dawn over flat roofs, the doorway and Rebekah's travelling cloak; the mother's age isn't given (24:55-58).
The nurse not 'old' (no age given, 24:59); removed the city wall and gate, the green plain and the long caravan: ten camels (24:10, 24:61); added the servant's men.
Added Rebekah's nurse and damsels and the servant's men, who came with her (24:59, 24:61); removed the orange sky; Isaac is forty (25:20).
Removed the servant unloading the camels and the starry night; Isaac brings Rebekah to his mother Sarah's tent (24:67).
Removed Isaac and Keturah (not said to be there) and the sons' wives, children and flocks; Keturah's six sons sent away east with gifts (25:2, 25:6).
Removed Isaac and Ishmael kneeling at the bedside and the household outside; the text says only that Abraham died, old and full of years (25:8).
Removed the servants bearing the body and the beam of light on Isaac (an invented sign: 'God blessed' him, 25:11, without appearing), so god is n; Ishmael about 89.
Not shown dying among his sons ('in the presence of all his brethren', 25:18, is unclear); removed the camels and herds; twelve princes, towns and strongholds (25:16).
Removed Isaac praying by the well below (his prayer, 25:21, came before she conceived), the night sky and hilltop; Rebekah married nearly twenty years (25:20, 25:26).
Removed the two midwives and Isaac (not said to be there) and the dawn; the first twin red and hairy, the second holding his heel (25:25-26).
Removed the rope Jacob was mending and the midday sun; Rebekah an older woman now, the twins grown men (25:27-28).
Removed Esau's bow dropped in the dirt and the reddening sky; Esau swears, then Jacob gives him bread and pottage of lentils (25:33-34).
Removed the household and thin flocks (only Isaac is named) and the twilight stars: the stars are in God's promise (26:4), not in the scene.
Abimelech now by his cast key; removed the palace garden and fig tree; Rebekah fair but no longer young, long married (26:7-8, 25:20-26).
Removed the guards, townspeople, heralds and Rebekah: Abimelech called Isaac (26:9); his charge to all his people (26:11) is not pictured.
Removed the radiant beams (an invented sign: 'the LORD blessed him', 26:12, is no appearance), so god is n; 'barley' made grain, as the crop isn't named.
Removed the Philistines filling the wells as Abimelech speaks (they had stopped them earlier, 26:15, 26:18) and the camels; Abimelech by his cast key.
Removed the midday glare and the staffs shaken in anger; the herdsmen strive with words, 'The water is ours' (26:20), and Isaac is among them.
Removed the golden evening and green pasture (neither in the text); Isaac by the well no one strove for (26:22).
The altar, tent and well came after the night appearance (26:24-25): removed them and the servants with lanterns; Isaac alone with the light.
Removed the escort of soldiers (the text names three men, 26:26), Phichol's armour and the windy afternoon; Abimelech by his cast key.
Removed the remains of the feast on rugs and the party riding; Abimelech's party departs in peace (26:31) as the servants report water (26:32).
Removed the wives' kinsmen bearing gifts, the jewellery and the onlooking household; Esau forty (26:34), Rebekah no longer young.
Removed the early dawn and misty hills (no time is given); Isaac old and blind (27:1), Esau about 77.
Rebekah grown old, married about 97 years (25:20, 25:26; Jacob about 77); removed the goat pens and the two kids shown, as the flock was elsewhere (27:9).
Rebekah grown old, not young (25:20, 25:26; Jacob about 77); removed the noon light; the skins on his hands and neck (27:16).
The goatskins are on his hands and neck (27:16, 27:22-23), not his arms; removed the afternoon sunbeams.
Removed the grain fields and vineyards beside the tent and Isaac's hands on Jacob's head; Jacob kisses Isaac, who smells his raiment and blesses him (27:26-27).
Jacob had already gone out (27:30): removed him slipping away and the windswept sunset; Isaac trembles once Esau names himself (27:32-33).
Removed the gathering storm clouds and the servants watching from the shadows (not in 27:34-40).
Removed Esau brooding on a ridge (his words were told to Rebekah, 27:42), the moonlit night and the packed bundle (Isaac sends Jacob later, 28:5).
Removed Rebekah (not in 28:1-5), the dawn and the bundle; Jacob about 77 (47:9, 41:46, 45:6, 30:25), a man in his prime.
Removed Nebajoth giving her away and the watching tribe, palms and spring (not in 28:9); Ishmael, dead by now (25:17), is not shown.
The sun had already set (28:11), not setting in an orange blaze; removed the bundle.
A ladder, as the KJV says (28:12), not a shining stairway; the angels kept low on it; the LORD as light above it (28:13), not flooding the land.
Removed the hilltop, the mist in the valleys and the slopes of Luz (a city only named, 28:19); the stone set up and oil poured on it (28:18).
Removed the lone shade tree and the stone's round shape (only 'a great stone', 29:2); the shepherds wait for all the flocks to gather (29:8).
Removed the brimming troughs (none at this well in 29:2-10), the drifting clouds and the shepherds' astonishment; Jacob kisses Rachel and weeps aloud (29:11).
Removed Rachel with her sheep and the servants and neighbours in doorways (not in 29:13); Laban runs out to meet Jacob and brings him home (29:13).
Removed the courtyard well, the spring morning and Rachel's shy glances; Laban's two daughters only, Leah tender eyed and Rachel beautiful (29:16-17).
Removed the music and long tables (29:22 has only a feast) and the 'bridal tent'; Leah brought to Jacob in the evening (29:23), Zilpah given to her (29:24).
Removed the servants clearing the feast who stop to stare; only Jacob, Laban and Leah (29:25-26).
Removed the canopy of branches, the cedar chest, the gathering and Leah watching in sorrow; Laban gives Rachel, and Bilhah as her maid (29:28-29).
Removed the beam of light on her tent (an invented sign: the LORD opened her womb, 29:31, without appearing), so god is n; removed Rachel watching.
Removed Leah's little sons playing nearby (not in 30:1-4) and the hot afternoon.
Removed the women of the household gathering round and the sunset; only Rachel, Bilhah and Bilhah's two sons, Dan and Naphtali (30:5-8).
Removed the women of the camp clapping and singing and Leah's four sons among the goats; only Leah, Zilpah and her two sons, Gad and Asher (30:10-13).
Removed the reapers and Jacob coming home, which is that evening (30:16); Reuben a small boy: Jacob's eleven sons in Haran came within seven years (29:30, 30:25, 31:41).
Removed the beam of light (God hearkening, 30:17, is no appearance), so god is n, and the busy camp; six young sons and newborn Dinah (30:20-21).
Removed the column of light (God remembering Rachel, 30:22, is no appearance), so god is n; removed Jacob, Bilhah and the women, and the night.
Removed the wives, children and maids ready to leave (Jacob only asks to go, 30:25-26) and his pointing west.
Laban's sons not 'grown' (their age isn't given, 30:35); removed the cool, cloudy morning.
Removed the newborn speckled lambs (brought forth later, 30:39) and the evening shadows; rods of poplar, hazel and chestnut (30:37).
Removed the hazy summer day and the tents; Jacob's stronger flocks kept apart from Laban's feebler ones (30:40-42), with his servants, camels and asses (30:43).
